claims.feature: other: sentimentality as a named risk
claims.claim: Oden reports that critics sometimes fault Kay for being too sentimental and too romantic, and partly concedes the charge.
claims.source: Scott Oden (novelist), 'A Quarter Turn', Towers of Spider-Haunted Mystery (Substack), 2026
claims.quote: Critics sometimes hit Kay for being too sentimental, too romantic
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'Critics sometimes hit Kay'

claims.claim: A tabletop-RPG forum reader says Kay's narrator commentary and foreshadowing often felt heavy-handed to him.
claims.source: 'Uqbarian', post #19 in 'Talk to me of Guy Gavriel Kay', RPGnet forum, 2022
claims.quote: his narrator commentary and foreshadowing often felt really heavy-handed to me

claims.claim: The same reader says Kay is a top-notch prose stylist who goes on rather more than he needs to.
claims.source: 'Uqbarian', post #19 in 'Talk to me of Guy Gavriel Kay', RPGnet forum, 2022
claims.quote: he just goes on rather more than he needs to

claims.claim: The same reader reports a scene in The Lions of Al-Rassan of characters thinking portentous thoughts for five and a half pages.
claims.source: 'Uqbarian', post #19 in 'Talk to me of Guy Gavriel Kay', RPGnet forum, 2022
claims.quote: thinking portentous thoughts for five and a half pages

claims.claim: Another forum reader says the renamed real cities of The Last Light of the Sun left him constantly mixing up not-Constantinople and not-Jerusalem.
claims.source: 'Daztur', post #10 in 'Talk to me of Guy Gavriel Kay', RPGnet forum, 2022
claims.quote: constantly get not-Constantinople and not-Jerusalem mixed up

claims.claim: A forum reader says The Lions of Al-Rassan moves between an adventure story and a people-living-through-history story.
claims.source: 'Gavin Bennett', quoted post in 'Talk to me of Guy Gavriel Kay', RPGnet forum, 2022
claims.quote: a sort of adventure story and a people living through history

claims.claim: A reviewer says that while he enjoys Kay's prose he often wishes there was less of it.
claims.source: 'Brok3n Engines', review of Tigana, Brok3n Engines (Substack), 2025
claims.quote: while I enjoy his prose, I often wish there was less

claims.claim: Kay says the subject engaging him is that a novel you read is a story being told to you by someone.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed by Patrick St-Denis, Pat's Fantasy Hotlist, 2019
claims.quote: a story being told to you by someone
claims.page: answer to 'So what interests a more mature ... Kay nowadays?'

claims.claim: Kay says he is fascinated by how we examine and remember the past and shape the narratives we need from it.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed by Patrick St-Denis, Pat's Fantasy Hotlist, 2019
claims.quote: how we examine and remember the past
claims.page: answer to 'So what interests a more mature ... Kay nowadays?'

claims.claim: Kay says he would be more an architect than a gardener because the shape of a novel matters a lot to him.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed by Patrick St-Denis, Pat's Fantasy Hotlist, 2019
claims.quote: the shape of a novel matters a lot to me

claims.claim: Kay says setting came first for A Brightness Long Ago.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed by Patrick St-Denis, Pat's Fantasy Hotlist, 2019
claims.quote: I think setting came first here
claims.page: answer about A Brightness Long Ago's arc of emergence

claims.claim: The interviewer reports Kay having said that in general setting precedes theme, which grows out of learning about time and place.
claims.source: Patrick St-Denis (interviewer), paraphrasing Kay's earlier answer, Pat's Fantasy Hotlist, 2019
claims.page: interviewer's question about A Brightness Long Ago

claims.claim: Kay warns readers to be sceptical when writers present intuitive processes as thought-out planning.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'On the Strengths of Fiction Done as Near-History' (first published at boingboing.net, 2016), Bright Weavings
claims.quote: be skeptical when writers present intuitive processes as thought-out planning
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'There are a multiplicity of reasons'

claims.claim: Kay says he always includes starter bibliographies in his novels.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'On the Strengths of Fiction Done as Near-History' (first published at boingboing.net, 2016), Bright Weavings
claims.quote: And I always include starter bibliographies
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'And I found that I liked'

claims.claim: Kay says each reader makes the book they read.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'On the Strengths of Fiction Done as Near-History' (first published at boingboing.net, 2016), Bright Weavings
claims.quote: each reader makes the book they read
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'And I found that I liked'
